source_en: Returning to the residential block after the morning shift at the mine.
Collecting the weekly coal allocation for the eastern apartments.
End of shift at Coal Face B. Nothing to report.
The east shaft was sealed this morning. I'm going home.
Collecting protective gear from the depot before the next rotation.
Double shift at C shaft. I need to sleep.
The mine is closed. All of them. I'm just going home.
Nowhere else to go. The mine is shut.
Going home to the east block. My wife waits up.
Office clerk at the textile mill. Home for lunch.
Picking up my first wage packet. Started at the mine Monday.
Going home to an empty flat. Never married, no children.
Starting my shift at the east shaft. Coal Face B, as usual.
Sitting the university entrance exam. Mining engineering.
Visiting my sons in the east block. I live in the west.
The mine is running fine. I need to get back underground immediately.
Retired from the mine ten years ago. Visiting the old crew.
I heard the foreman call my name. He needs me back down there.
Long shift. Papers are in order.
Just off the morning rotation. Coal Face B.
I know I'm dirty. The showers at the shaft were out again.
They moved us to C shaft. Longer walk.
Eleven hours today. I don't complain.
The ventilation has been bad this week. We manage.
They closed the mine. I don't know what I'm supposed to do now.
Just going home.
I used to know what my day was.
Good. Thank you.
Right. Thank you.
Alright.
I haven't done anything wrong. I just want to sleep.
You're keeping me from my bunk, officer.
Fine. I've been in smaller places.
I... didn't think... it would end like this.
I've survived worse... collapses...
...I should have stayed... underground...
I've slept in mine shafts tighter than this. I'll manage.
No need to explain. I'll wait. I know how to wait.
The walls are concrete, not rock. But it's the same in the dark.
Thirty years underground... gas pockets... collapses... and this...
Tell my wife... she knows... she always knew...
I thought... it would be the mine... that got me...
Where are you coming from?
The mine. Coal Face B, east shaft. Morning rotation. Going home to the east block.
C shaft. They sealed the east one. Eleven hours. Longer walk.
Nowhere. The mine is shut. I walked to the gate and stood there. Now home.
The tram depot. I drive the number four line. Twelve years now.
Coal Face B, east shaft. Same as always. Normal shift, nothing to report.
The station. Saw my wife off on the Tbilisi train. I live alone now.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
Coal dust. Always coal dust. The mine doctor says my lungs are fine.
Some dizziness. Ventilation in C shaft is bad. It passes.
Tired. More than usual. I do not sleep without the shift. The cough is the same.
Nothing. I am thirty-one. The body does not complain yet.
Nothing. The air in C shaft is the best in the mine. New fans. Clean.
Never coughed in my life. I kept the ledgers in the mine office. Never went down to the face.
B shaft today. Long one.
I know I smell. The showers at the mine were out again.
Papers are in order. Always are.
They moved us to C shaft. Longer walk. Worse air.
Three men on my crew did not show this morning. Nobody said anything about it.
I do not complain. I just want to get through.
The mine is closed. First time in thirty years I have had nothing to go back to.
Just going home. That is all.
I used to know what my day was.
